<thought>Based on the NMR data, the molecule contains four methyl groups (total 12 H) all appearing as singlets, and three distinct carbon signals in the aromatic/unsaturated region (≈161, 144, 130 ppm) with four methyl carbon signals (≈26.6, 22.8, 21.4, 19.2 ppm). This pattern matches a highly symmetric, fully substituted aromatic system bearing four methyl groups and a carbonyl substituent, giving the formula C₁₁H₁₂O. The most plausible structure is 1‑acetyl‑2,4,5‑trimethylbenzene, whose SMILES is “CC(=O)c1c(C)cc(C)c(C)c1”. This SMILES reproduces the observed NMR features (acetyl methyl = 6 H singlet, three aromatic methyl singlets, and the three aromatic carbon signals). 

Thus the SMILES string for the sample is: 

CC(=O)c1c(C)cc(C)c(C)c1</final_answer>
